title: How the wmti Lua plugin is used
description: The usage path end to end: invoke, configure, open, discover, drive, step. For learning to use wmti, not modify it.

steps.title: The verbs you can run
steps.why: open / next / prev / close / select / dive — the entire command surface, one table you can read at a glance.

steps.title: One :Wmti, dispatched
steps.why: The first argument is the verb (defaulting to open); each maps to a module function, which is what lets the plugin lazy-load on first use.

steps.title: What you configure
steps.why: Just three knobs — which side, how wide, and which directory to scan — set once via setup{} or your lazy.nvim opts.

steps.title: Open adapts to what it finds
steps.why: The open flow adjusts to your project: zero walkthroughs just notify, exactly one opens straight in, several drop you into a picker.

steps.title: Where it looks
steps.why: It globs .wmti/*.json under your working directory, so discovery only finds anything when you launch Neovim from the project root.

steps.title: Keys you drive it with
steps.why: The sidebar binds n/p/Tab/Enter/q buffer-locally and keeps focus, so you step through the tour without ever leaving the panel.

steps.title: Each step jumps your window
steps.why: Each step loads its file into your existing main window (not a new split) and centers the line it points at.

steps.title: Why it survives edits
steps.why: It re-locates each step by its anchor text, so even after the code moves the reader still lands on the right lines.
